versions.short: The bill would extend through fiscal year 2031 several federal programs that fund research and development of drugs and other treatments for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, also called Lou Gehrig's disease) and other brain and nerve diseases. It would continue grants from the National Institutes of Health for research on experimental drugs for people who cannot otherwise join clinical trials, and grants from the Food and Drug Administration for developing treatments for ALS and similar diseases. It would also continue a public-private partnership between the FDA and NIH to help develop and review such treatments. When considering renewing its grants, the NIH would have to review available information on how safe and effective the experimental drugs are and require grantees to promptly report serious, unexpected side effects. In addition, the FDA would have to publish a five-year plan for encouraging safe and effective drugs for ALS and other rare neurodegenerative diseases and for making experimental drugs easier to access, and later publish a report on the actions it has taken under that plan.
